title: Tenant credit shadowing from ingestion replay race across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private reported unexpected credit deductions followed by late reversals. Initial symptom: tenant dashboards showed negative transient credit spikes and then a set of automated refunds ~6–12 hours later. Customers reported confusing billing changes and one enterprise customer escalated to legal due to spike in monthly usage. This ticket tracks investigation, immediate mitigation, fix, and backfill plan.
impact: High: 4 enterprise customers affected, intermittent overcharging on monthly invoices, potential revenue recognition risk and elevated churn risk for one strategic account.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate high-concurrency streaming requests from single session across a proxy and a direct dedicated node (mix hosted/dedicated routing).
2) Force a transient network partition on the ingest service leading to retries from client-side SDK (we used internal stress harness)
3) Observe ingestion events being replayed with new request IDs but same session_id; check ledger rows for duplicate token counts
4) Trigger a dedicated node eviction/failover to exercise cross-deployment attribution mapping
5) Run reconciliation job and verify offset corrections appear as delayed refunds
root_cause: Race between streaming ingestion replay logic and ledger deduplication. Idempotency key generation currently uses per-request proxy ID which changes when a request is retried or routed across deployments. Replayed events bypassed an eventual-dedupe window because the ledger uses a time-window-based watermark which was out-of-sync across regions; this allowed duplicate token rows to be written and later removed by a reconciliation job that detects high-confidence duplicates, producing the late refunds. Dedicated routing differences (session-to-tenant mapping) caused some duplicates to be created only in Dedicated or Private deployments, making the effect non-uniform across customer environments.
proposed_fix: 1) Change idempotency to derive from stable session_id + model_snapshot + token-stream-hash (server-calculated) so retries produce the same key across proxies and deployments. 2) Add a strict DB unique constraint on (tenant_id, session_id, idempotency_key) with a safe migration strategy. 3) Tighten the reconciliation watermark logic and make it region-aware so ledgers don't rely on a single global sliding window. 4) Add defensive dedupe in the ingestion hot-path that checks recent KV cache before writing ledger rows.
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): Deploy idempotency change & KV cache check to Hosted region us-west-2 only (2-day canary) with feature-flag off for Dedicated/Private. Phase B: Enable feature-flag for a small set of Dedicated customers behind opt-in. Phase C: Ship DB migration to add unique index and backfill in a maintenance window (low traffic). Phase D: Enable reconciliation watermark change globally. For Private deployments, provide a patch bundle and migration script; coordinate with SEs and schedule on-customer maintenance windows.
backfill_plan: 1) Freeze reconciliation (pause automated refunds) while we verify duplicated rows list. 2) Run a safe aggregation job to compute per-tenant net delta and generate signed audit CSVs. 3) Apply customer credits via billing pipeline for verified overcharges and create manual invoices where needed. 4) Notify affected customers with an itemized audit and remediation ETA. Estimated total credits: ~USD 12,400 across 4 customers. Backfill job runbook in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/billing/backfill-2026-03
monitoring_playbook: - Dashboards: datadog:/dashboards/usage-ledger-dedup and datadog:/dashboards/reconciliation-latency. - Alerts: fire when per-tenant refund-rate > 0.5% of hourly token consumption or when reconciliation job flags >1000 candidate duplicates. - Add a temporary emergency alert to paging channel #platform-billing when credits are applied via backfill. - Post-deploy: monitor 24/7 for 72 hours with on-call rotation and daily stakeholder updates.
